0.0.n: Here it introduces the update rather than answering a question.

0.2.n: Sets the time for the statement that follows.

0.3.n: 時 marks the hour and 半 adds thirty minutes; evening is understood from context.

0.4.n: A polite ending used here to state the time.

1.0.n: Names the evening meal and is the subject of 終わり.

1.1.n: Marks 夕食 as what has ended.

1.2.n: The connecting form of 終わる links dinner ending to the next completed activity.

1.4.n: An English loanword that combines with リセット to name the cleanup routine.

1.5.n: Here it means cleaning and tidying the kitchen back into its usual ready-to-use state.

1.6.n: Marks キッチンリセット as the activity that has finished.

1.7.n: The polite past form of 終わる describes something coming to an end.

2.0.n: Here it refers to washing items by hand, not washing your hands.

2.1.n: Links 手洗い to もの, describing the items by how they are washed.

2.2.n: A general word for things; the unfinished phrase leaves the rest understood from context.

3.0.n: Adds another point to the speaker’s update.

3.2.n: Gives the day when the curry was made.

3.3.n: Marks 今日 as the topic, framing the statement around today.

3.4.n: Describes cooking with moisture from the ingredients rather than adding water.

3.5.n: Describes the style of curry, not the location where it was made.

3.6.n: The long vowel mark ー is part of this loanword’s spelling.

3.7.n: Marks the curry as what the speaker made.

3.8.n: The plain past form of 作る comes before ので to explain the reason.

3.9.n: Connects making the curry with the resulting action of putting some into containers.

3.11.n: This chunk contains これだけ plus 作り, the first half of 作り置き, meaning food prepared for later.

3.12.n: Completes 作り置き with the preceding 作り; read them as one word rather than separately.

3.13.n: Marks 作り置き as the role of the portion being stored: food prepared for later.

3.14.n: Combines with 容器 to describe a container used for keeping food.

3.15.n: Japanese does not specify here whether there is one container or more.

3.16.n: Marks 保存容器 as the destination where the food is placed.

3.17.n: The polite past form of 入れる describes placing something inside something else.

0.tip: ８時半 gives the time but does not itself specify morning or evening.

1.lit: Dinner ended, and the kitchen reset finished.
1.tip: 終わり connects the two events, while 終わりました supplies the polite past ending.

2.tip: 手洗いの describes the items’ washing method; the phrase alone does not say whether washing is already finished.

3.lit: Also, today, because I made no-added-water hotel-style curry, I put just this much into storage containers as make-ahead food.
3.tip: Read 作り置き as one word meaning food prepared for later, even though the displayed chunks split it.
